findings.excerpt: Henry Meller came to Costa Brava for round two occupying last place in the 2013 TEG Wooden Spoon race
An opening round of +7 net vs par had put him there.
The third brought a double bogey.
The par-5 fourth brought a triple.
The fifth brought another double.
From the 9th to the 12th he gained five shots against net par and dropped not one gross shot.

findings.excerpt: The swing from his opening effort was 12 shots.
It was the best gross round recorded by anyone in the field that day.
His net score was also the weakest of the round.
The turnaround lifted him off the bottom of the Wooden Spoon race.
Stuart Neumann now occupies it, presumably wondering how.
Gregg Williams arrived at Club de Golf Costa Brava on 22 September 2013 leading the TEG Trophy.
An opening round of net -12 had earned him the privilege.
The front nine was a procession of bogeys, interrupted only by a quadruple bogey at the 7th, the hardest hole on the course.
The stretch from the 9th to the 12th read rather better than it looked. Four more bogeys, but with handicap strokes attached they banked him four shots against the field.
From the 13th to the 16th he shed 11 gross shots without recording a single net par.
A birdie at the 17th, the easiest hole, finally broke the run of bogey-or-worse.
